Subject and Object Relative Clauses to express time and place

When you want to clarify which person or thing you are talking about, you use a relative clause. We use relative clauses to give additional information about something without starting a new sentence.
You can begin a relative clause with who for people, which for things or that for either people or things.
You can begin a relative clause with when for time and where for place.
You put the relative clause immediately after the noun it talks about.
A subject relative clause describes the subject of the clause and comes after the subject of the sentence.
An object relative clause describes the object of the clause and comes after the object of the sentence.
Relative Adverbs
Relative adverbs are used like relative pronouns:

When = is used for a time: The time when I went to the workshop.
Where = is used for a place: The workshop where I learned about cover letters.

It was emphasized when I did the workshop.
(It was emphasized then.)

The cover letter is where you give a more personal introduction.
(You give a more personal introduction there.)

How to Write a Cover Letter

A cover letter must be sent with your résumé when you apply for a job.
Below are some tips on how to write a great cover letter.
Parts of a good cover letter

• Meet and greet (first paragraph). Concisely explain how you found out about this job lead and explain that you would like to apply for the job. Note generally what you do to qualify you for consideration. Be sure to use language that signals you pay attention to details, conveys professionalism, and demonstrates your written communication skills.

  • Skills and experience profile (second and third paragraphs). Offer a short profile of your skills and expertise and highlight any accomplishments that would get this employer's attention.

  • Reason to Interview (fourth paragraph). Make clear why your particular abilities could make a difference for this company in this position. Show you've done your research into the company in this paragraph and thought how your capabilities are strong match for the job. In short, give this company a reason to call you up for an interview.

  • Promise to follow up (last paragraph). Close by thanking the company for reviewing your résumé and promise to follow up with a short call to learn more about the position.
Cover letter guidelines

• Keep it concise, usually one page.
  • Ask a reliable source to read and edit your cover letter before you send it.
  • Write multiple drafts, editing and revising as you go.
  • Use bullet points if you can, itemizing your skills or job experience.
  • Keep the formatting simple, using basic fonts.
A cover letter must be sent with a résumé.
The letter should have four paragraphs.
The first paragraph should explain how you found out about this job lead and explain that you would like to apply for the job.
The second paragraph is a short profile which highlights your skills, experiences and achievements.
The third paragraph makes it clear why your particular abilities could make a difference for this company in this position.
The fourth paragraph closes the letter by thanking the company for reviewing your résumé and promise to follow up with a short call.
You also need to remember to research the company and address the letter to a specific person, including their title.
